doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Latin influence and raising children in New York
summary: She mentions Spanish ancestry and Latin friends in California, and how hard schooling children in New York was.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It’s interesting because some of those things early on seem to have come out in your playing and compositions, the Latin thing and—

Also I think, I don’t know what percentage, but I have some Spanish in me on my father’s side, so that I don’t know whether — well California has a lot of people who speak Spanish. They are not Spanish, they are more Mexican, but of course I had a lot of friends like that.
Was it difficult raising children in New York?

At the time you know we just made it. We just made it. There was a few schools left and you kind of had to give an address of a friend to get them in the right schools that were left. But just about the time they graduated I would say that it would be very difficult to raise them now, and school them the way that you want them schooled without a whole lot of money. It would have to be done privately. Things may change, but it was on the cusp. I had to move them from the school they should have gone to to one that was good. And they made it through.
